newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up, first time in eight sessions.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up, first time in eight sessions.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared earlier gains on Tuesday as short-covering and a technical rebound faded, traders said, but closed up for the first time since November 13.
"Early buying petered out. Part of it was short-covering in Telmex and GCarso stocks, the rest of it was due to bargain hunting and a technical rebound," said a trader.
The blue-chip IPC index closed up 24.80 points, or 0.76 percent, at 3,271.45. Volume was much improved on many recent sessions at 101.01 million shares traded.
Three cross trades accounted for some 12 million shares traded which inflated volume, but dealers said trade was healthy even so.
"It's the kind of volume we like to see," said Ramon Ruiz, sales trader at Bankers Trust in New York.

Other traders pointed out that Mexican stocks were buoyed up by ADRs listed in New York. Telmex ADRs ended up 3/8 at 30, while its heavily weighted L series shares gained 16 centavos to 11.88 pesos in Mexico.
On the broad market, a total of 110 stocks changed hands, of which gains easily outnumbered losses by 59 to 33.
Two series of shares in cellular phone company Iusacell headed the leaders, following news Bell Atlantic was to assume management control of the company.
Autoparts firm Iasasa followed Iusacell, up two centavos at 33, following news of a debt restructuring plan by the company's creditors.
Beverage firm Ggemex led the losers after closing down 30 centavos at 2.50 pesos.
